questions.text: Which pairing describes the core Transfusion-style training design?

options.A: Text uses diffusion loss; discrete image codes use text classification loss.
options.B: Text uses next-token loss; continuous image representations use denoising loss.
options.C: Text and images both use next-token loss over discrete image codebook IDs.
options.D: Text and images both use pixel reconstruction loss without a vocabulary.

questions.explanation: A shared transformer combines autoregressive cross-entropy for discrete text with a diffusion or denoising objective for continuous image representations.

questions.text: Which attention pattern supports causal text generation while allowing patches in one noisy image to coordinate denoising?

options.A: Fully bidirectional attention over all text and all images.
options.B: Fully causal attention everywhere, with no within-image exceptions.
options.C: Each image patch attends only to itself, while text sees future tokens.
options.D: Causal text attention with bidirectional attention within each image block.

questions.explanation: Text must not access future text targets, while patches in the same noisy image block can attend bidirectionally to coordinate image denoising.

questions.text: The toy train loop computes losses, then executes text_scale += 1 and img_scale += 1 without gradients. What does this demonstrate?

options.A: Loss accounting with scripted scale changes, rather than learned gradient updates.
options.B: Backpropagation through the shared transformer using an implicit optimizer.
options.C: Independent gradient descent on two complete pretrained model backbones.
options.D: Automatic optimization of loss weights using validation-set accuracy.

questions.explanation: The scales increment unconditionally. No differentiation or optimizer applies gradients from the computed loss, so this is a simulation of loss plumbing.
